plan_revision.verification_note: All external claims verified against vendor docs on 2026-08-28. No code in this repository has been compiled or executed; the sandbox has no JDK, Gradle or Android SDK. All latency figures are targets, not measurements.

architecture_type: Privacy-First On-Device GPU-Resident Frame Pipeline (Media3 effect chain + LiteRT)
executive_summary: Video UpScaler AI enhances local video entirely on device, with no cloud dependency. Frames never become CPU Bitmaps. Enhancement is implemented as a shared list of Media3 GlEffect stages that runs inside a single GL pipeline: ExoPlayer hosts it for real-time preview, Media3 Transformer hosts it for offline export, so preview and export cannot drift visually. Super-resolution runs through the LiteRT GPU delegate (OpenCL). True zero-copy HardwareBuffer interop is a Phase 2 C++ objective using the LiteRT CompiledModel API, not a Kotlin property of Phase 1.
architecture_pipeline_flow: Encoded Input MP4 (via Storage Access Framework)
Shared GlEffect chain on the GL thread: colour normalisation -> Lanczos base resample -> AiUpscaleGlEffect (LiteRT) -> temporal stabilizer -> CAS sharpen
Audio: passthrough or AAC re-encode (preserved, never dropped)

corrections_from_v1.claim_in_v1: Pass HardwareBuffer directly into interpreter.runForMultipleInputsOutputs for zero-copy GPU execution.
corrections_from_v1.finding: Interpreter.runForMultipleInputsOutputs accepts only multidimensional arrays or java.nio.Buffer types (ByteBuffer, FloatBuffer, IntBuffer, LongBuffer). android.hardware.HardwareBuffer is not supported. The v1 blueprint does not work.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Phase 1 uses an explicit two-copy path (glReadPixels -> direct ByteBuffer -> delegate -> GL texture). True zero-copy is deferred to Phase 2 via the C++ CompiledModel API (TensorBuffer::CreateFromGlBuffer, kLiteRtTensorBufferTypeAhwb).

corrections_from_v1.claim_in_v1: Insert LiteRT inference between MediaCodec decoder and encoder; chunk the video via Media3 Transformer.
corrections_from_v1.finding: Transformer exposes no seam for external per-frame processing; it is a closed decode->encode pipeline. Also, Transformer.Builder.setVideoEffects() was removed in Media3 1.6.0.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Inference lives inside a custom GlEffect / BaseGlShaderProgram (queueInputFrame), which Media3 documents as the extension point (its own example runs a MediaPipe FrameProcessor there). Effects are attached via EditedMediaItem.Builder.setEffects(Effects(...)) and transformer.start(editedMediaItem, path).

corrections_from_v1.claim_in_v1: FastSRGAN (a GAN) as the flagship quality path.
corrections_from_v1.finding: GAN super-resolution hallucinates detail from a single frame; run per frame it produces visible temporal shimmering, which requires multi-frame alignment to suppress. No model in the v1 matrix does this.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Tiers are ordered by temporal determinism. ESPCN-class (near-deterministic) becomes the default. GAN SR is opt-in, requires a motion-gated temporal stabilizer, and carries a user-facing warning. A new Tier 0 (Media3 built-in LanczosResample + CAS) is the universal, flicker-free floor.

corrections_from_v1.finding: Arithmetically wrong. 1280x720 at 2x is 1440p and at 4x is 2880p; 720p->1080p is 1.5x. Sub-pixel CNNs support integer scale factors only, so 1.5x requires 2x followed by a downsample.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Model matrix now states input resolution, integer model scale and explicit post-scale step. 4x is removed from v1 (a 2880p intermediate is ~177 MB of tensor memory on a phone).

corrections_from_v1.finding: Contradicts the plan's own 35-55 ms/frame figure (18-29 fps ceiling before decode/encode) and its WorkManager background-job design.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Tagline drops 'Real-Time'. Live preview is real-time (Tiers 0/1). Export is offline and progress-driven (Tiers 2/3).

corrections_from_v1.claim_in_v1: Pipeline flow makes no mention of audio.
corrections_from_v1.finding: Audio was absent from the entire v1 plan; an upscaler that outputs silent video is broken.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Audio passthrough / AAC re-encode policy added, plus multi-track selection and A/V sync verification at any boundary.

corrections_from_v1.claim_in_v1: Wrap compute in a generic ForegroundService with a persistent notification.
corrections_from_v1.finding: Android 15 added a purpose-built mediaProcessing foreground service type for exactly this workload. dataSync and mediaProcessing services are limited to 6 hours per 24-hour period (shared across the app's services of that type), after which onTimeout() is called and failure to stopSelf() throws RemoteServiceException; starting a new one with the budget exhausted throws ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Use mediaProcessing (API 35+) with dataSync as the Android 14-and-below fallback; implement onTimeout(); track the 6-hour budget; write fragmented MP4 with checkpoints so long exports resume.

corrections_from_v1.claim_in_v1: org.tensorflow:tensorflow-lite 2.14.0; NNAPI delegate on the MobileSR row.
corrections_from_v1.finding: TensorFlow Lite is now LiteRT (com.google.ai.edge.litert:*). NNAPI was deprecated in Android 15 and the Play-services LiteRT package ships no NNAPI delegate at all.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Migrate coordinates (litert 1.4.2 for the Interpreter line, minSdk 21; 2.2.0 for CompiledModel, minSdk 23, NDK r26a). Remove NNAPI; use the GPU delegate.

corrections_from_v1.claim_in_v1: Stated latencies such as ~12-18 ms/frame and ~35-55 ms/frame.
corrections_from_v1.finding: No harness, device or methodology exists; these are unmeasured assertions.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Retained only as labelled Phase 0 targets, with a measurement gate that must pass before the architecture is committed.

corrections_from_v1.claim_in_v1: Primary risk is LMK terminating the process above a RAM threshold.
corrections_from_v1.finding: A mediaProcessing foreground service is largely protected from LMK; the real failure modes are elsewhere.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Replaced with a 12-entry risk register covering in-pipeline inference cost, flicker, FGS budget, GPU OOM, thermal throttling, colour/range handling, driver-specific delegate failures, model licensing, temp storage, HDR, A/V sync and Play policy.

corrections_from_v1.finding: Stale by roughly two years. Media3 stable is 1.11.0 (2026-08-05).
corrections_from_v1.correction: Pinned to current versions; the Media3 1.6.0 effects API break is called out explicitly.

corrections_from_v1.claim_in_v1: Chunk video into 5-10 second blocks via Media3 Transformer to bound RAM.
corrections_from_v1.finding: Transformer already streams decode->effect->encode incrementally, so memory is bounded without cutting the file. Chunking the encode forces an IDR at every boundary (bitrate spikes, visible seams) and requires concatenation.
corrections_from_v1.correction: Chunking demoted to a contingency, to be used only if measurement shows a real memory problem, and then only on keyframe boundaries. Crash recovery is handled instead by fragmented MP4 plus presentation-timestamp checkpoints.

production_pillars.name: GPU-Resident Frame Pipeline
production_pillars.description: Never materialise video frames as CPU Bitmaps. Frames stay as GL textures inside a Media3 GL pipeline. Phase 1 accepts a two-copy bridge into the delegate; Phase 2 targets true zero-copy via the C++ CompiledModel API.
production_pillars.honesty_note: Do not describe Phase 1 as zero-copy. It is not.

production_pillars.name: One Effect Chain, Two Hosts
production_pillars.description: A single List<Effect> defines 'enhanced'. ExoPlayer.setVideoEffects hosts it for preview; EditedMediaItem.setEffects hosts it for export. This makes the comparison slider honest and removes preview/export visual drift.

production_pillars.name: Determinism-Ordered Adaptive Tiers
production_pillars.description: Tiers are ranked by temporal determinism, not raw sharpness: Lanczos+CAS (universal, flicker-free) -> FSR 1.0 EASU/RCAS shader -> ESPCN sub-pixel CNN (default AI) -> GAN SR (opt-in, stabilized, warned). Capability detection picks the tier; any delegate init failure falls through.

production_pillars.name: Temporal Consistency
production_pillars.description: Frame-independent super-resolution shimmers. A motion-gated temporal stabilizer is on by default for the GAN tier and available for the AI tier. This is a quality requirement, not a polish item.

production_pillars.name: Resumable Background Export
production_pillars.description: WorkManager schedules; a mediaProcessing foreground service executes; fragmented MP4 with presentation-timestamp checkpoints makes interruption recoverable. The 6-hour per-24-hour service budget is tracked and surfaced to the user.

production_pillars.name: Measure Before You Commit
production_pillars.description: A benchmark and quality harness (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS against bicubic and Lanczos references, fixed clip set) exists before the first UI screen. Every quality claim must be reproducible.

capability_tiers.name: Lanczos + CAS
capability_tiers.implementation: Media3 built-in LanczosResample / Presentation + custom CAS sharpen GlEffect
capability_tiers.role: universal floor; always ships; also the fallback for every failure mode

capability_tiers.name: FSR 1.0 EASU + RCAS
capability_tiers.implementation: GLSL ES 3.0 shader port of AMD FSR 1.0 (MIT-licensed)
capability_tiers.role: low-end SoC, battery saver, real-time preview

capability_tiers.name: ESPCN sub-pixel CNN

capability_tiers.role: opt-in 'max detail' mode with an explicit user-facing warning; never the default

verified_media3_api.note: Signatures below checked against the androidx.media3 API reference on 2026-08-28.
verified_media3_api.BaseGlShaderProgram_constructor: BaseGlShaderProgram(boolean useHighPrecisionColorComponents, int texturePoolCapacity) - takes NO Context and NO useHdr flag
verified_media3_api.configure: abstract android.util.Size configure(int inputWidth, int inputHeight) - returns the OUTPUT size
verified_media3_api.drawFrame: abstract void drawFrame(int inputTexId, long presentationTimeUs) - the synchronous per-frame hook
verified_media3_api.queueInputFrame: void queueInputFrame(GlObjectsProvider glObjectsProvider, GlTextureInfo inputTexture, long presentationTimeUs) - override only for asynchronous work
verified_media3_api.GlTextureProducer: exposes only releaseOutputTexture(long presentationTimeUs); has no width/height and no Listener.Releasable
verified_media3_api.output_signal: outputListener.onOutputFrameAvailable(GlTextureInfo, long presentationTimeUs); owner must return it via releaseOutputFrame(GlTextureInfo)
verified_media3_api.LanczosResample: NO public constructor. Created only via the static factories scaleToFit(int width, int height) and scaleToFitWithFlexibleOrientation(int firstDimension, int secondDimension). Use the flexible-orientation form so portrait video upscales to 1080x1920 instead of being letterboxed.
verified_media3_api.Transformer.Listener: onCompleted(Composition, ExportResult), onError(Composition, ExportResult, ExportException), onFallbackApplied(Composition, TransformationRequest, TransformationRequest) - all default methods.
verified_media3_api.ExportException: public final int errorCode is a FIELD; the error NAME is a method getErrorCodeName(), not a field.
verified_media3_api.ProgressHolder: public @IntRange(0,100) int progress is a FIELD. Poll Transformer.getProgress(ProgressHolder); it returns a @Transformer.ProgressState int.

implementation_code_blueprints.export_wiring:
val chain = listOf(
    // LanczosResample has NO public constructor - static factory only.
    LanczosResample.scaleToFitWithFlexibleOrientation(targetLong, targetShort),
    AiUpscaleEffect(model, scale = 2, blend = 0.7f),
    TemporalStabilizeEffect(strength = 0.3f),
    CasSharpenEffect(amount = 0.35f),
)

// Preview
exoPlayer.setVideoEffects(chain.filter { it.isRealtimeSafe })

// Export. NOTE: Transformer.Builder.setVideoEffects() was REMOVED in Media3 1.6.0.
val edited = EditedMediaItem.Builder(MediaItem.fromUri(inputUri))
    .setEffects(Effects(/* audioProcessors = */ emptyList(), /* videoEffects = */ chain))
    .build()

Transformer.Builder(context)
    .setVideoMimeType(MimeTypes.VIDEO_H265)
    .setAudioMimeType(MimeTypes.AUDIO_AAC)   // audio is preserved; v1 never mentioned it
    .setHdrMode(HDR_MODE_TONE_MAP_HDR_TO_SDR_USING_OPEN_GL)
    .addListener(exportListener)
    .build()
    .start(edited, outputPath)
threading_rules: Create the interpreter on the GL thread and invoke it only from that thread; the LiteRT GPU delegate throws 'GpuDelegate must run on the same thread where it was initialized' otherwise.
The EGLContext must be current on the invoking thread for the delegate's GL path; BaseGlShaderProgram.queueInputFrame already satisfies this.
Create the interpreter once and reuse it; never construct per frame.
Reuse one set of textures and one PBO across frames; per-frame allocation dominates runtime.
implementation_code_blueprints.why_v1_blueprint_failed: v1 passed android.hardware.HardwareBuffer instances into interpreter.runForMultipleInputsOutputs, which accepts only multidimensional arrays or java.nio.Buffer types (ByteBuffer, FloatBuffer, IntBuffer, LongBuffer). The call cannot work as written.

zero_copy_phase2.gate: Only begin after Phase 0 proves the two-copy path is too slow on target devices.
zero_copy_phase2.cost: A C++/NDK project: build system, JNI, ABI splits, and a second code path to test.
zero_copy_phase2.mechanism: LiteRT 2.x CompiledModel API. TensorBuffer::CreateManaged(env, kLiteRtTensorBufferTypeAhwb, ...) yields an AHardwareBuffer-backed tensor; .GetGlBuffer() and .GetOpenClMemory() expose it to GL and OpenCL with no copy. Ordering uses an EGL sync fence event instead of a CPU wait.

register.risk: In-pipeline inference too slow due to two-copy overhead
register.mitigation: Phase 0 gate; ship Tiers 0/1 if it fails; zero-copy only if justified by measurement
Tier 3 opt-in; temporal stabilizer; tiers ordered by determinism
Implement onTimeout(); track the budget; fragmented MP4 checkpoint and resume

register.risk: GPU OOM from large intermediate textures
register.mitigation: Cap target resolution by RAM class; reuse textures; 4x removed from v1

register.risk: Thermal throttling after several minutes of full GPU load
register.mitigation: Phase 0 sustained-thermal test; adaptive tier downgrade under thermal pressure

register.risk: Colour or range shift (BT.601 vs BT.709, limited vs full range)
register.mitigation: Explicit colour handling in the effect chain plus a colour-accuracy clip in the harness

register.risk: Delegate initialisation throws on specific GPU drivers
register.mitigation: CompatibilityList plus a catch-all fallback to Tier 1, per device

register.risk: Model weight or training-dataset licensing blocks shipping
register.mitigation: Verify per model before bundling; prefer self-trained weights; record provenance in MODEL_CARD.md

register.risk: Temp storage exhaustion from multi-GB intermediates
register.mitigation: Pre-flight free-space check; stream instead of buffering; clean up on cancel
Tone-map to SDR via Media3; HDR output out of scope for v1
No encode chunking (v1 pillar 3 demoted); A/V sync test in the harness

register.risk: Play policy on background processing and storage permissions
register.mitigation: SAF-only file access; mediaProcessing service type; no MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE

risk_mitigation.superseded_v1_note: v1's only risk was LMK termination above a RAM threshold. A mediaProcessing foreground service is largely protected from LMK, so that framing understated the real failure modes.

assets.status: clear to port; retain the notice
verify the released checkpoint and its training set before bundling
prefer training your own on a permissively licensed corpus

licensing.recommendation: Train ESPCN in-house and ship your own FP16 weights. It removes the licensing question, costs little (ESPCN trains in hours), and yields a model tuned to real phone video rather than DIV2K crops. Check DIV800/DIV2K-Flickr2K licensing per use if those sets are used.

kept_from_v1: On-device only, no cloud - correct and differentiating; keep as the headline
Never decode frames into Bitmap - correct instinct; the mechanism was wrong, not the goal
Adaptive capability-based fallback - correct; strengthened by ordering tiers by determinism
Foreground service with a persistent notification - correct; corrected to mediaProcessing plus budget handling
Comparison slider UX - correct; now trustworthy because preview and export share one effect chain
open_questions: Is the Play-services LiteRT runtime acceptable, or must the delegate be bundled for non-Play devices?
Ship models in the APK or via Play Asset Delivery? Depends on final model sizes versus the base module limit.
Is 1080p the hard ceiling for v1, or is 1440p expected? This materially changes the memory budget.
Monetisation model - affects whether Tier 3 is a paid tier and how models are delivered.
Is a temp-space pre-flight check sufficient, or is user-visible storage UI required?
